instructions: Independently verify each claim using authorized source and original reproducible evidence. Do not quote publisher material into public artifacts. Signature proof alone does not grant approval.

subjects.author_claim: A superclass constructor can dynamically dispatch to an overriding method before subclass fields receive their explicit initialization.
subjects.independent_challenge: Explain why an explicitly initialized final subclass field may still be observed with its default value during base construction.

subjects.author_claim: A superclass operation that calls an overridable method makes that call sequence observable to subclasses, possibly doubling instrumentation.
subjects.independent_challenge: Distinguish subclass hook calls from direct caller operations; demonstrate an override that changes counting.

subjects.author_claim: A protected extension hook is part of a supported inheritance contract and cannot be treated as a freely changeable implementation detail.
subjects.independent_challenge: Identify what the superclass must document about invocation order, errors and thread context.

subjects.author_claim: A final class prohibits subclassing; sealed types restrict authorized subtype declarations but do not themselves document safe override protocols.
subjects.independent_challenge: Test a final extension rejection, then explain why sealed alone cannot make an unsafe virtual constructor call safe.

subjects.author_claim: A Java class may implement multiple independent interfaces while extending one superclass.
subjects.independent_challenge: Build a class retaining a required base type and two capability interfaces.

subjects.author_claim: An interface cannot provide a default implementation of equals(Object) overriding the Object-method signature.
subjects.independent_challenge: Compile a deliberately illegal interface and distinguish abstract redeclaration from default implementation.

subjects.author_claim: Inheriting conflicting unrelated interface defaults requires an explicit resolution in the implementing class.
subjects.independent_challenge: Prove a conflict is rejected without an override and resolved with one.

subjects.author_claim: A skeletal implementation can offer shared state and method implementations while interfaces keep capabilities open to other implementation lineages.
subjects.independent_challenge: Distinguish an optional skeletal helper from a mandatory base class.

subjects.author_claim: Synchronizing each primitive operation separately does not establish atomicity for a default compound operation invoking several primitives.
subjects.independent_challenge: Require an interleaving argument; distinguish per-call lock possession from an enclosing batch lock.

subjects.author_claim: A missing whole-batch lock establishes lack of a guarantee, not proof that a concrete race happened.
subjects.independent_challenge: Demand a schedule or counterexample trace before asserting an observed race.

subjects.author_claim: Adding a default method can violate behavioral assumptions of an existing interface implementation even when its source still compiles.
subjects.independent_challenge: Inspect a wrapper rather than asserting every standard JDK implementation is affected.

subjects.author_claim: An interface default may be overridden by an implementing class to restore a required behavioral invariant.
subjects.independent_challenge: Contrast inherited implementation and an explicit synchronized batch override.

subjects.author_claim: Implementing a constants-only interface introduces constant names into the implementing type’s inherited API surface.
subjects.independent_challenge: Examine name exposure without claiming that interface constants become mutable instance fields.

subjects.author_claim: Fields declared in an interface are implicitly public, static and final; implementations cannot assign to them.
subjects.independent_challenge: Compile a rejected attempted assignment and separate type design from mutability.

subjects.author_claim: Enums provide stable typed identities; an int constants holder does not provide the same type discrimination.
subjects.independent_challenge: Explain a stable outcome enum without promoting every numeric configuration setting to enum status.

subjects.author_claim: A changing financial threshold belongs in validated runtime policy rather than in hard-coded enum constants.
subjects.independent_challenge: Give a rollback-sensitive policy example and state why a static configuration enum would be inappropriate.

subjects.author_claim: A tagged class can admit combinations of tag and fields that are invalid for a particular variant.
subjects.independent_challenge: Construct an inconsistent state; compare with variant-specific representations.

subjects.author_claim: A sealed hierarchy limits permitted subtypes but does not automatically validate field values in permitted record implementations.
subjects.independent_challenge: Instantiate an invalid unvalidated record and prove an explicit canonical constructor rejects it.

subjects.author_claim: A record holding a mutable array is not deeply immutable merely because its component fields are final.
subjects.independent_challenge: Demonstrate array aliasing and propose defensive copying on input/output.

subjects.author_claim: A Java 21 switch over a known sealed hierarchy may be exhaustively checked, while missing a permitted variant can fail compilation.
subjects.independent_challenge: Run a nonexhaustive switch negative fixture without implying exhaustive cases validate fields.

subjects.author_claim: A nonstatic member-class constructor requires an enclosing instance in this Java 21 language and compiler setup.
subjects.independent_challenge: Reflect over constructor parameters, separately from fields on the created instance.
subjects.java_baseline: Java 21; cross-compiler details must be checked independently

subjects.author_claim: The tested Java 21 javac can omit an unused synthetic outer-instance field on a nonstatic member class.
subjects.independent_challenge: Reflect over an unused-owner member class; do not universalize this implementation optimization.
subjects.java_baseline: Java 21; cross-compiler details must be checked independently

subjects.author_claim: A nonstatic member class that actually accesses enclosing instance state retains a reference in the tested Java 21 compiler output.
subjects.independent_challenge: Demonstrate a real outer access and inspect fields; avoid using GC timings as proof.
subjects.java_baseline: Java 21; cross-compiler details must be checked independently

subjects.author_claim: A static member class does not require an implicit owner instance to be constructed.
subjects.independent_challenge: Contrast constructor signatures, not only source spelling.
subjects.java_baseline: Java 21; cross-compiler details must be checked independently

subjects.author_claim: Java permits distinct package-private top-level classes to share one compilation unit.
subjects.independent_challenge: Positive-compile two distinct package-private types together.

subjects.author_claim: A public top-level class must be declared in a compilation unit named for that class under ordinary javac source-file compilation.
subjects.independent_challenge: Negative-compile a public type in a mismatching filename.

subjects.author_claim: Duplicate top-level declarations with the same fully qualified name are rejected when compiled together.
subjects.independent_challenge: Distinguish duplicate class from merely colocated distinct classes.

subjects.author_claim: One top-level type per source file is a maintainability convention, not a universal Java grammar requirement.
subjects.independent_challenge: Explain why recommending a convention differs from claiming a compile-time ban.
